issues.description: Field SealSaloon.totalOrders: The problem UML (problem_statement.md) declares totalOrders as type int, but the reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) declares totalOrders as a long. This discrepancy between 'int' in the specification and 'long' in the solution can confuse students about the expected type and the getter return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of SealSaloon.totalOrders consistent across artifacts. Either change the UML/problem text to specify 'long totalOrders' and ensure any examples/use match long, or change the reference implementation to 'private int totalOrders' and adjust its getter to return int. Update the problem statement UML, textual description, and the solution/template code to use the same type.

issues.description: Field SealSaloon.stock visibility/initialization: The problem text instructs students to have a final Stock stock initialized in the instance constructor (an instance final field), but later in the same problem it requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is not possible. The reference implementation declares stock as 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' (initialized at declaration). This contradictory guidance (initialize in constructor vs make static) prevents a clear correct implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and choose one design: (A) Require an instance-level final Stock: remove the statement that stock must be static and instruct students to initialize 'private final Stock stock' in the no-arg constructor, or (B) Require a class-level shared Stock: specify 'private static final Stock stock' and instruct students to initialize it at declaration or in a static initializer (and remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor). Update the UML, all textual instructions, and example code to reflect the chosen option.
